moved.sentence: Define each external dependency as a protocol the app owns, not a concrete type the vendor owns

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD defining each external dependency as a protocol the app owns, not a concrete type the vendor owns.

moved.sentence: Keep adapter implementations thin — translate and delegate, never add business logic

judged.note: should-keep-adapters-thin keeps thin translate-and-delegate adapters at SHOULD, and must-not-add-business-logic-to-adapters makes never adding business logic a MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: If two modules need to share a type, extract it into a shared contract rather than coupling the modules directly

judged.note: The rule keeps the two-modules-share-a-type condition and extracting a shared contract rather than coupling the modules directly at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Verify boundaries by confirming core logic compiles and tests pass with no framework imports

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD verifying boundaries by confirming core logic compiles and tests pass with no framework imports.

moved.sentence: Extend at the boundary, don't break the contract: once a boundary is stable and widely depended on, add capability through new implementations behind the port rather than changing the port's existing shape — the durable kernel of the open/closed principle.

judged.note: should-extend-at-the-boundary keeps the stable-and-widely-depended-on condition and adding capability behind the port rather than changing its shape; rationale keeps the open/closed kernel.

moved.sentence: Apply it only to boundaries that have actually stabilized; do not pre-generalize one you are still discovering (see yagni, steel-thread-first).

judged.note: should-not-pre-generalize-unstable-boundaries keeps applying it only to stabilized boundaries and not pre-generalizing one still being discovered, with the yagni and steel-thread-first pointers.
